answer: In a marketplace where agents survey a basalt ledge above a canyon, each bidding identity must lock $500 in escrow for 30 days before submitting offers. The bond stays locked even if the identity leaves, so an attacker cannot recycle one deposit through a stream of aliases. Running 1,000 eligible identities requires tying up $500,000 at once, making a sybil swarm costly without claiming each account is a unique person.
